requirements.summary: A modern, high-fidelity landing page featuring complex scroll-driven animations, sticky positioning, text reveal effects, and continuous UI mockup animations. The design uses a sophisticated light green and dark green color palette with a mix of serif and sans-serif typography.
requirements.template_goal: Build a reusable, highly animated landing page template with centralized configuration for scroll-spy sections, text reveal sequences, and feature cards.
hard_constraints: The hero section must include a continuous, smooth animation of the UI cards on the right side.
The 'Specialties' section must use a sticky layout where the right side remains fixed while the left side scrolls through the list.
The 'Problem/Solution' section must implement a scroll-driven text highlight effect.
The converging lines animation must trigger on scroll and resolve into a single line.
All animations must be tied to scroll position where appropriate, or use IntersectionObserver for enter animations.

section_requirements.name: Navigation
styling: CTA button: dark green background, white text, rounded-full

section_requirements.name: Hero
section_requirements.purpose: Introduce the product with a strong value proposition and visual demonstration.
section_requirements.layout: Two-column grid (text left, visual right) with a full-width logo strip below.
styling: CTA: dark green, rounded-full, flex with arrow icon
UI Mockup: floating cards with shadows, rounded-lg
copy_items: Admit more patients, reduce staff burden, and get paid faster with an AI-native system built for behavioral healthcare.
assets: Investor logos (Andreessen Horowitz, Abstract, Maven, etc.)
UI Card components (CRM, EHR, RCM, Emma Smith)
behaviors: Continuous animation: The 'Emma Smith' card moves between the CRM, EHR, and RCM slots, simulating data flow.

section_requirements.name: Sticky Scroll Features
section_requirements.purpose: Highlight supported specialties while keeping core value props visible.
section_requirements.layout: Two-column layout. Left column scrolls, right column is sticky.
must_include: Sticky content area with tag, headline, and stats
styling: Left list items: large text, muted green when inactive, dark green background with white text when active
Right content: tag with light green background, serif headline, large stat numbers
copy_items: Ease is built from the ground up for behavioral health practices, with AI at the core.
behaviors: Scroll-spy: As the user scrolls down, the active item in the left list changes styling.
Sticky right column: The right side remains fixed in the viewport while the left side scrolls.
Text highlight: The headline on the right highlights specific words sequentially.

section_requirements.name: Problem and Solution Reveal
section_requirements.purpose: Contrast the current fragmented state with the unified solution.
section_requirements.layout: Centered, single-column layout with large typography.
styling: Text: serif, large, dark green. Unhighlighted text has lower opacity or a lighter color.
copy_items: Fragmented CRM, EHR, and RCM systems are inefficient. They slow intake, burden staff, and hide revenue leakage.
Instead of bouncing between CRM, EHR, and RCM systems, Ease provides one AI-powered system for referrals, clinical notes, and billing.
behaviors: Scroll-driven text reveal: Words or lines highlight (opacity increases or background highlight appears) as the user scrolls through the section.
Line animation: Multiple horizontal lines draw in from the left and converge into a single line on the right as the user scrolls past the solution text.

section_requirements.name: Benefits Cards
styling: Cards: light green background (--bg-primary), rounded-lg, padding, dark green text
copy_items: Consolidate intake, clinical notes, and billing into one unified record without painful integrations.
AI-assisted intake, automated assessments, and billing workflows empower teams to do more.
A robust billing engine and expert services run in the background so you never miss a claim.
behaviors: Fade-in up: Cards animate into view sequentially when the section enters the viewport.

layout_requirements: Use a max-width container (e.g., max-w-7xl) for main content to ensure it doesn't stretch too far on ultra-wide screens.
Implement CSS Grid for the hero section and benefits cards.
Use CSS Flexbox for navigation and alignment within cards.
The sticky scroll section requires a parent container with relative positioning and a child with sticky positioning.
styling_requirements: Apply the defined color palette strictly. Avoid hardcoding hex values outside of the token definitions.
Use the serif font for major headlines and the sans-serif font for body copy, tags, and UI elements.
Ensure high contrast for text, especially when highlighting.
copy_requirements: Use exact copy provided in the section requirements.
Structure copy in a configuration object or JSON file if the framework allows, to make it easily editable.
asset_requirements: Use placeholder SVGs for logos and icons if exact assets are unavailable, but maintain the aspect ratio and visual weight.
The hero UI mockup should be built with HTML/CSS rather than a static image to allow for the required animations.
behavior_requirements: Implement smooth scrolling for anchor links if any.
Ensure the sticky section un-sticks cleanly when the user scrolls past its parent container.
The text reveal effect should be tied to scroll progress (e.g., using Framer Motion's useScroll or a similar library/custom hook).
animation_requirements: Hero Mockup: Create a looping animation where a 'patient card' translates horizontally and vertically between three 'system' columns. Use CSS keyframes or a motion library.
Text Reveal: As the user scrolls, transition text color from a muted state to the primary dark green state. This should happen progressively.
Converging Lines: Animate SVG paths. Start with multiple parallel horizontal lines that animate their `d` attribute or use a mask to reveal a pre-drawn converging shape based on scroll position.
Benefits Cards: Trigger a staggered fade-in and translate-y animation when the section intersects the viewport (threshold ~0.2).
structure_guidance: Break the page into distinct semantic sections: <header>, <main>, <section id='hero'>, <section id='specialties'>, <section id='problem-solution'>, <section id='benefits'>.
Use a dedicated component for the scroll-spy list to manage active state logic cleanly.
Use a dedicated component for the text reveal effect to encapsulate the scroll-tracking logic.
execution_plan: 1. Setup project structure, define CSS variables/Tailwind config based on design tokens.
3. Build the Hero section layout and typography.
4. Implement the Hero UI mockup HTML/CSS and its continuous looping animation.
5. Build the Sticky Scroll Features section layout (left scroll, right sticky).
6. Implement the scroll-spy logic to highlight left-side items based on scroll position.
8. Implement the scroll-driven text reveal animation for the Problem/Solution text.
9. Create the SVG converging lines and animate them based on scroll.
10. Build the Benefits Cards section and implement the intersection observer fade-in.
11. Review responsive behavior across all sections, ensuring sticky logic and animations degrade gracefully on mobile.
known_unknowns: The exact easing curves and timing for the hero animation are estimated.
The specific SVG paths for the converging lines animation need to be approximated.
Mobile layout behavior is not shown in the video; assumptions will be made for responsive degradation (e.g., stacking the sticky section).

interaction_checkpoints.name: Hero Animation Loop
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The Emma Smith card moves continuously between the CRM, EHR, and RCM columns.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Specialties Scroll
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The left list scrolls up. The right content remains fixed. The active list item gets a dark green background.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Problem Text Reveal
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The text 'Fragmented CRM...' highlights progressively as the user scrolls.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Converging Lines
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: Multiple horizontal lines animate into a single line.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Benefits Reveal
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The three feature cards fade in and slide up.

acceptance_criteria: The page matches the provided color palette and typography.
The hero section contains a continuously animating UI mockup.
The specialties section has a working sticky right column and a scrolling left column with active state highlighting.
The problem/solution text highlights progressively on scroll.
The converging lines animation triggers on scroll.
The benefits cards animate into view when scrolled to.
The layout is responsive and does not break on smaller screens.

validation.summary: The candidate is exceptionally close to the reference, successfully implementing complex scroll-driven animations, sticky layouts, and continuous loops. The primary remaining issues are minor styling and spacing discrepancies in the Specialties list.
strengths: Excellent implementation of the continuous Hero UI mockup animation using CSS keyframes.
Smooth and accurate scroll-spy and sticky behavior in the Specialties section.
Correct implementation of the scroll-driven text reveal effect.
Highly editable structure using a central configuration object and CSS variables.

issues.title: Incorrect active state colors for Specialty items
issues.observed: The active item in the Specialties list has a dark green background with white text.
issues.expected: The active item should have a light green background with dark green text to match the reference video.
issues.fix_instructions: In the `<style>` block, update the `.specialty-item.active` rule to use `background-color: var(--bg-primary);` and `color: var(--text-primary);`.

issues.title: Excessive spacing in Specialties list
issues.observed: The items in the Specialties list are spaced too far apart vertically, and have excessive horizontal padding.
issues.expected: The list items should be stacked more tightly, with moderate padding around the text.
issues.fix_instructions: Locate `<div id="specialtyList" class="flex flex-col gap-10">` and change `gap-10` to `gap-2`. For all `.specialty-item` children, change `px-10` to `px-6` and `py-3` to `py-2`.

patch_instructions: In the `<style>` block, find the `.specialty-item.active` CSS rule. Change its `color` property to `var(--text-primary)` and its `background-color` property to `var(--bg-primary)`.
Locate the `<div id="specialtyList">` element. Change its `gap-10` class to `gap-2`.
Within the `#specialtyList` container, update all child `<div>` elements (the specialty items) by replacing the `px-10` class with `px-6` and the `py-3` class with `py-2`.
